blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415). The r418-r421 shutdown hang is FIXED and LIVE-VERIFIED (r422), with automated regression coverage added (r424). Separate, not-yet-fixed discovery from r424: HEAD has never been buildable from a byte-for-byte fresh clone (native_vulkan_backend.cpp has never had Vulkan linkage in any committed CMakeLists.txt) -- named for a dedicated future cycle. r427 found the ROOT CAUSE of presented_frames=0/present=0 (r418, closed after r425/r426 byte-level-confirmed the symptom): read sub_821F03B0 (VdSwap's direct caller) and sub_821E4F88 (its ring-space-reservation helper, called just before VdSwap) in full. sub_821E4F88 only checks remaining ring capacity and returns the current write cursor -- it writes NOTHING to the buffer. The game then passes that cursor plus 6 more arguments (front buffer pointer, palette, dimensions -- exact field mapping not yet decoded) DIRECTLY to the VdSwap kernel call, with no PM4 packet ever constructed in guest code in between. This matches real Xbox 360 kernel behavior: VdSwap is a genuine syscall whose real xboxkrnl.exe implementation builds and injects the XE_SWAP PM4 packet from its arguments -- the game never writes that packet itself. Our host stub for VdSwap (tools/materialize_native_import_stubs.py) only reads ctx.r3 (for bookkeeping via publish_write_address) and discards ctx.r4 through ctx.r10 entirely -- it never synthesizes or injects any PM4 packet. This is not a retail game bug or anything related to the r399-r422 allocator/threading chain -- it's a localized, incomplete host-side kernel stub implementation. Named for r428: decode the exact semantics of VdSwap's 7 arguments (the stack structures sub_821F03B0 builds at r1+96/100/104/108/116/128/208), then design, apply, and live-verify a fix that has the VdSwap stub actually construct and inject a valid XE_SWAP PM4 packet at the reserved cursor before calling publish_write_address. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched beyond what r422 already swept in -- reports and named tool/source changes for r413-r427 were committed individually.
